source_text: Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo atque argumentis opus non est. Probatio est ad fidem facilis compendio veritatis. Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni coelorum: et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Super illum unum aedificat Ecclesiam suam, et illi pascendas mandat oves suas. Et quamvis Apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos: accipite Spiritum sanctum; si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi, si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen, ut unitatem manifestaret, unam cathedram constituit, unitatis ejusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri Apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, et primatus Petro datur, ut una Christi Ecclesia et cathedra una monstretur. Et pastores sunt omnes, et grex unus ostenditur, qui ab Apostolis omnibus unanimi consensione pascatur, ut Ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam Ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Hanc Ecclesiae unitiatem qui non tenet, tenere se fidem credit? Qui Ecclesiae renititur et resistit, qui cathedram Petri, super quem fundata est Ecclesia, deserit, in Ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: Unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes vocationis vestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus.
pass_a_gloss: If someone considers and examines, a long treatment and arguments are not needed. The proof to faith is easy by the compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: I say to you, he says, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not conquer it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and what you will have bound on earth, will be bound also in heaven; and whatever you will have loosed on earth, will be loosed also in heaven. And again he says to the same one after his resurrection: Feed my sheep. On that one alone he builds his Church, and he entrusts his sheep to be fed to him. And although he gives equal power to all the Apostles after his resurrection and says, As the Father has sent me, and I send you: receive the Holy Spirit; if you will have remitted the sins of anyone, they will be remitted to them, if you will have retained those of anyone, they will be retained, nevertheless, so that he may manifest unity, he establishes one chair, the origin of his unity beginning from one by his authority he arranges. These things were indeed also the other Apostles what Peter was, endowed with equal partnership and honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that one Church of Christ may be shown. Which one Church also the Holy Spirit designates and says in the Song of Songs in the person of the Lord: My dove is one, my perfect one is one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent. This unity of the Church, who does not hold, believes himself to hold the faith? Who resists and resists the Church and deserts the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, confides in being in the Church? when also the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity saying: One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God.

pass_b_english: If anyone considers and examines this, no long treatment or arguments are needed. The proof for faith is easy through the compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: "I say to you, he says, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not conquer it" (Matthew 16:18-19). "And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven" (Matthew 16:18-19). And again after his resurrection he says to the same one: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17). On that one alone he builds his Church, and he entrusts his sheep to him to be fed. And although he gives equal power to all the Apostles after his resurrection and says, "As the Father has sent me, so I send you: receive the Holy Spirit; if you remit the sins of anyone, they are remitted to them; if you retain those of anyone, they are retained" (John 20:21-23), nevertheless, so that he may manifest unity, he establishes one chair; he arranges by his authority the origin of that unity beginning from one. The other Apostles were indeed what Peter was, endowed with an equal partnership of honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that the one Church of Christ may be shown. Which one Church the Holy Spirit also designates and says in the Song of Songs in the person of the Lord: "My dove is one, my perfect one is one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent" (Song of Songs 6:9). This unity of the Church, who does not hold it, believes himself to hold the faith? Who resists and withstands the Church and deserts the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, confides that he is in the Church? When the blessed Apostle Paul also teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: "One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God" (Ephesians 4:4-6).
